scan_metadata.notes: Fresh shallow clone of default branch (depth 20); has_uncommitted_changes reflects the clone (false), not the author's working copy. Primary backend language is Go (261 files), which is out of scope for skill version 1.0: routes were enumerated by reading cmd/actalog/main.go (chi router) and auth was determined from the middleware groups (middleware.Auth, AdminOnly, CoachOrAdmin) shown there, but full interface/data-access detection for Go was not performed beyond that and targeted reads. The Go dependency manifest (go.mod, 'go' key) was added under dependencies in addition to python/node. Frontend is Vue 3 (JavaScript) in web/, with a Playwright suite in e2e/ and two small Python helpers under site/scripts. Routes under the authenticated groups have severity null (not severity-tagged) because auth_detected is true; only the 23 unauthenticated routes carry severity 'low'. Excluded from findings: test fixtures and example values (web/src/**/*.test.js passwords, internal/**/_test.go, e2e default credentials listed separately as low), docs/, site/, screenshots, minified or vendored third-party code, and woff2/png/pdf assets. Personal data in tracked files: imports/user_workouts_export_2025-12-22.json contains the author's email and workout notes, and imports/Performance_fromWodify6Nov2025.csv is a gym performance export; these are noted under sensitive_data_indicators. The repo root entry 'actalog' is a broken symlink to bin/actalog. Roughly 1389 SQL write and 586 read call sites exist; SQL access was sampled in internal/service/data_quality_service.go and backup_service.go rather than read in full.

sql_injection_risk.reason: internal/service/data_quality_service.go builds IN-clauses with fmt.Sprintf from IDs formatted by strconv.FormatInt (makeInClause), and backup_service.go interpolates table names from an internal list and column names filtered against target columns; no user-controlled string reaches the query text in the sampled code, so these are latent, not active. All other sampled queries use placeholders

docker_findings: docker/Dockerfile: multi-stage build, base images pinned by sha256 (node:24-alpine, golang:1.26-alpine, alpine:latest@sha256), USER actalog (non-root), EXPOSE 8080, HEALTHCHECK on /health, ENV DB_DRIVER=sqlite3 default

docker/docker-compose.yml: publishes 8080 on all interfaces, secrets via ${VAR} interpolation, healthcheck wget /health, named volumes for data and uploads; ADMIN_EMAIL/ADMIN_PASSWORD optional env vars for auto seed
docker/trouble/docker-compose.yml: MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD contains a password-shaped string in an error-message default (see critical finding); also uses version: '3.8' and the :latest image tag
Default configuration allows an empty JWT_SECRET unless APP_ENV=production (configs/config.go:185); default APP_ENV is 'development'
ALLOW_REGISTRATION defaults to true and REQUIRE_EMAIL_VERIFICATION defaults to false

what_this_app_can_do: Lets registered users log CrossFit workouts, track personal records, view progress charts, performance history, calendars and leaderboards, and import/export their data as CSV or JSON (authenticated; subscription required for write operations).
Lets anyone without a login register (when enabled), log in, reset a password, and browse the public catalog of standard movements, WODs and workout templates.

Lets admins manage users (create, disable, change role, force or set passwords, unlock), organizations, subscriptions, class scheduling, packages and documents, audit and email logs, data quality merges, announcements, and create/download/restore full database backups.
Lets coaches or admins view session rosters and check in or mark no-shows for class sessions.
Serves uploaded avatar files publicly at /uploads/* and public Swagger API documentation at /api/docs/*.

data_sources_touched.source: Application database (SQLite by default; PostgreSQL or MariaDB/MySQL selectable) holding users, workouts, WODs, movements, subscriptions, audit logs
Uploaded avatars and backup zips on local volumes (uploads, backups)
SMTP server (SMTP_HOST) used to send verification, reset and announcement emails
User-uploaded CSV imports (including a Wodify performance export) and CSV/JSON exports
youtube.com video links stored with WOD/movement entries

capability_summary.who_can_reach_it: Binds to 0.0.0.0:8080 by default and is designed to be reachable by any user who can reach the host (optionally behind a Caddy reverse proxy). Most routes require a JWT; the public routes are login/registration/password reset, version, Swagger docs, the standard movement/WOD/template catalog, /health and /uploads/*.
unauthorized_action_red_flags: docker/trouble/docker-compose.yml contains a password-shaped string tied to MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD in a tracked file.
Swagger UI (/api/docs/*) and the standard catalog are served without authentication.
JWT secret may be empty in non-production APP_ENV (default), which would make tokens forgeable if left unset.
Admin backup download/restore and user password-set endpoints exist (admin-only); a compromised admin account exposes the full database.
Tracked data exports contain personal data (author email and workout notes; a gym customer name).

top_findings: Critical: password-shaped string committed in docker/trouble/docker-compose.yml:22 (MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD error-message default), tracked and not gitignored
Low: tracked docker/.env.postgres, docker/.env.mariadb (placeholders) and web/certs/localhost-key.pem (dev key)
217 of 236 /api routes sit behind JWT middleware (120 admin-only); 19 public API routes plus /health, /uploads/*, / are recorded as low
JWT_SECRET may be empty unless APP_ENV=production; default bind 0.0.0.0; registration enabled by default
